clue.text: A role that is distinct

parts.note: an actor's role is a part in a play

explanation.surface: A theatrical role that stands out from the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Things set separate from one another are distinct, each standing alone.

clue.text: What tourists see in Athens — a harvest on poor soil

parts.note: a harvest is a crop gathered in

indicators.note: poor soil is in bad shape, so these letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A guidebook note on Greek farming: a scanty yield from thin ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' turns SOIL into OLIS, placed after A and CROP; 'on' simply joins the pieces in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient citadel holding the Parthenon is the chief sight visitors climb to in the Greek capital.

clue.text: Confirm Cartesian plan

indicators.note: to plan is to arrange, so the letters of the word before are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A request to verify a scheme laid out on Descartes's coordinate grid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cartesian plan' suggests the Cartesian plane of geometry, but 'plan' is the anagram signal on CARTESIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: To make certain of a fact by checking is to verify or confirm it.

clue.text: In which to see expert bowling analysis?

definitions.text: In which to see expert bowling analysis?

parts.words: In which to see expert bowling analysis?
parts.note: in cricket a bowler's analysis (wickets for runs) is most expert in the top-level international match format, not an examination of bowling skill

explanation.walkthrough: A bowling analysis is the cricket figure for a bowler, such as 5 for 40; the top international form of cricket is the five-day match between countries.
explanation.definitionFit: A Test match is the highest form of international cricket, where the finest bowlers record their figures.

clue.text: Heaven! Business enterprise meant to go broke!

parts.note: a business enterprise is a firm or company

indicators.note: to go broke is to be ruined, so the letters of the word before are smashed and reordered

explanation.surface: An exclamation of dismay at a company destined for bankruptcy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go broke' turns MEANT into AMENT, which follows FIRM.
explanation.definitionFit: The vault of the sky overhead, the heavens, is the poetic sense here.

clue.text: Contraption of magnificent fellow, in the air?

definitions.text: Contraption of magnificent fellow, in the air?

parts.words: Contraption of magnificent fellow, in the air?
parts.note: recalls the film about those magnificent men and their airborne contraptions, an early aircraft

explanation.walkthrough: The clue alludes to the 1965 film 'Those Magnificent Men in their Flying Machines', about an early air race from London to Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: An early aeroplane was a gadget for travelling through the sky, the vehicle of the film's daring aviators.

clue.text: Looking pale? Take a shot!

parts.note: a shy is a throw or attempt, as in a coconut shy, so a shot

explanation.surface: Someone looking washed out is told to have a go at something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take' is only a link here; a shy is a throw at a target, as at a fairground coconut shy.
explanation.definitionFit: Grey like the remains of a fire describes a pallid, drained complexion.

clue.text: Conspicuous effect of city area, almost at the last minute

parts.note: EC is the postcode area of the City of London

indicators.note: almost means not quite all of the word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: something done at the last minute is done late

explanation.surface: A tale of a striking show staged in the financial district just before the deadline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims LATE to LAT. EC is the postal district of London's financial City.
explanation.definitionFit: Brilliant display or striking success makes an impression on everyone watching.

clue.text: Underground right for such a plant?

parts.note: the London Underground is nicknamed the Tube

explanation.surface: A question whether a plant growing below ground is the proper kind.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tube is London's Underground railway. The answer is strictly a swollen root of a plant such as a potato, so the definition is loose, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A potato or dahlia grows from a fleshy storage stem buried in soil, the thing the clue hints at.

clue.text: Strains of Harrow school's opening

parts.note: to harrow is to torment or distress, as to rack is

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, taken here from the word for school

explanation.surface: Tensions at the famous Harrow public school as its term begins.
explanation.walkthrough: Harrow is a famous English public school, but here it is the verb meaning to torture.
explanation.definitionFit: To rack something is to stretch or strain it, as on the torture frame.

clue.text: Centre in which adolescents stick together?

definitions.text: Centre in which adolescents stick together?

parts.words: Centre in which adolescents stick together?
parts.note: a stick can be a club, so a place where young people gather is read as teenagers combined with a cudgel

explanation.walkthrough: 'stick together' suggests bonding, but a stick is also a club.
explanation.definitionFit: A community facility where teenagers meet for activities is a social centre for the young.

clue.text: Insured, can not come to harm-that's natural

indicators.note: letters that come to harm are damaged and broken up, so they appear in a new order

explanation.surface: An insurance claim saying an insured item cannot be damaged, which is only to be expected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'come to harm' scrambles INSURED CAN NOT together; 'that's' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Behaviour free of restraint or stiffness is spontaneous and unforced, which is natural.

clue.text: Standard quarter-cut

parts.note: par is the standard or normal level
E for east is one of the four quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: A butcher's usual cut of a quarter of beef.
explanation.walkthrough: A compass quarter is one of N, E, S or W.
explanation.definitionFit: To trim away the skin or edge of something is to cut it back.

clue.text: Light meal for number in bed

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for number inside the word for bed

parts.note: the sack is slang for bed, as in hit the sack

explanation.surface: Breakfast in bed for one of a number of guests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' suggests a figure, but it is the abbreviation N.
explanation.definitionFit: A small bite between proper meals, such as a sandwich, is a light meal.

clue.text: Heavenly body like Madonna?

explanation.surface: A query whether a heavenly being resembles the Virgin Mary.
explanation.definitionFit: A shining sun in the night sky; also a celebrity performer such as the pop singer Madonna.

clue.text: Gleaming silver common?

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
common in the sense of vulgar is low

explanation.surface: A question whether shiny silver is a commonplace metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Glowing with warm light describes something shining or gleaming.

clue.text: Cereal one kept in labyrinth

indicators.note: kept in means held inside, so the numeral sits within the word for labyrinth

parts.note: a labyrinth is a maze
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A breakfast-cereal box lost somewhere in a maze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cereal' sounds like a breakfast food, but here it is the crop, which also sounds like the labyrinth word.
explanation.definitionFit: Corn, the grain crop, is a cereal plant.

clue.text: Eve, maturing, turned out contentious

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Eve, maturing, turned out contentious', gives anagram fodder EVEMATURING (11 letters), which lacks the T and A needed for the 13 letters of the answer; no source found for the missing word

clue.text: Blissful state of innocence

parts.note: plays on the saying that not knowing is bliss, describing a happy lack of knowledge

explanation.walkthrough: The proverb runs 'where ignorance is bliss, 'tis folly to be wise' (Thomas Gray).
explanation.definitionFit: Not knowing things leaves one untroubled, the happy unawareness of the proverb.

clue.text: Hide outside?

parts.note: hide reads as the verb to conceal, but it is skin, and the outer layer of skin is meant

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide' looks like a verb telling someone to conceal themselves out of doors; it is the noun meaning skin.
explanation.definitionFit: The outer layer of skin is the surface covering of the body.

clue.text: Oldie taking higher subject

parts.note: senior means higher in rank
a subject of a state is a citizen

explanation.surface: An older student taking a subject at a higher level.
explanation.walkthrough: 'subject' suggests a school course, but it is a member of a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: An elderly person, often a pensioner, is an old person, colloquially an oldie.

clue.text: French duke goes to king for nothing

parts.note: duc is the French word for duke
K is the abbreviation for king in chess and cards

explanation.surface: A French nobleman yields to his monarch and gains nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a score of zero is a duck.
explanation.definitionFit: A batsman out without scoring makes a duck, a score of zero.

clue.text: Adorns ship's platforms

explanation.surface: Someone decorating the floors of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: To deck out is to decorate or adorn; a vessel's floors are its decks.

clue.text: Film I made of South American animal

parts.note: a film is a thin coating or layer, a coat

explanation.surface: A director describes the wildlife documentary about a South American creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Film' looks like a movie, but it is a thin layer.
explanation.definitionFit: A raccoon-like mammal with a long snout from Central and South America.

clue.text: Gold sovereign?

parts.note: reads as the British gold coin, but means a monarch whose touch turned everything to gold

explanation.walkthrough: A sovereign is an old British gold coin; here it is a king from Greek legend.
explanation.definitionFit: The Phrygian king of myth was granted a touch that turned all things to gold.

clue.text: Fare from France (by rail, that is)

parts.note: BR stands for British Rail
ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A traveller's note on food from France and on going by train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fare' suggests a train ticket, but it is food. British Rail (BR) was the UK's national railway.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft French cheese is an item of food from that country.

clue.text: Composer in rubber gloves

indicators.note: in signals that the letters sit inside the run of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A musician who performs wearing rubber gloves.
explanation.definitionFit: Alban Berg was an Austrian composer of the Second Viennese School.

clue.text: Party in the Italian image

indicators.note: in places the word for party inside the Italian article

parts.note: il is the Italian for the
a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: A party appearing in an Italian picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A statue worshipped as a god is a graven image.

clue.text: Fickle person slices up each lemon

indicators.note: slicing up the words chops their letters and rearranges them

explanation.surface: An unpredictable cook chops up every lemon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slices up' rearranges EACH LEMON.
explanation.definitionFit: A lizard famous for changing colour gives its name to someone who keeps changing views.

clue.text: Strong stuff from England's openers in bad light

indicators.note: in puts the opening letters inside the word for poor light

parts.note: bad light is dim
the opening letters of the word England are E and N

explanation.surface: England's opening batsmen stand at the crease in bad light, a cricket scene.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, openers are the first two batsmen and bad light stops play; here 'openers' are the first two letters of England.
explanation.definitionFit: A tough cotton twill used for jeans is a strong fabric, stuff being old word for cloth.

clue.text: Barking people require such a leg-protector

definitions.text: Barking people require such a leg-protector

parts.words: Barking people require such a leg-protector
parts.note: barking reads as a place or a dog, but to bark is to scrape the skin of the lower leg, against which a pad protects

explanation.walkthrough: Barking is a district of east London, but here it means scraping the skin, as in barking your shins.
explanation.definitionFit: A pad worn on the front of the lower leg in football or hockey protects it from kicks.

clue.text: Wise to leave wild edelweiss in city

indicators.note: wild means the letters of the flower name run free in a new order

explanation.surface: A sensible plan to leave wild alpine flowers growing in a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to leave' tells us the letters of WISE come out of EDELWEISS; 'wild' rearranges what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeds is a large city in West Yorkshire, England.
